model.rationale: Recent polls consistently show Talarico ahead by 2-4 points, prediction markets price him near 70%, and Paxton faces heavy outside opposition spending, all pointing to a narrow Democratic edge in an open seat. Texas's -6 partisan lean keeps the race close enough that modest polling error could flip it.
model.watch: Turnout composition in a record early-vote electorate, and whether Paxton consolidates Republicans in the final days, could narrow or erase the Democratic edge.
notes: Open seat: John Cornyn (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's open Senate seat has become one of the cycle's marquee contests, with state Rep. James Talarico facing Attorney General Ken Paxton after Paxton ousted incumbent John Cornyn in the primary. Recent polls from mid-to-late October show Talarico leading by roughly two to four points, and prediction markets give him about a 70% chance of winning. Most expert raters call the race a Tossup, though several lean Democratic.

Talarico holds an enormous financial advantage, having raised over $146 million, while Paxton has drawn more than $27 million in outside spending against him. Still, Texas's Republican-leaning fundamentals and the possibility of late Republican consolidation keep this competitive; a narrow Talarico win is the most likely outcome, but polling error in either direction could decide it.
